question: What is Bayes' theorem?
title: Bayes: Update Your Belief
hook: A positive test, yet only 8% are sick?
answer: Bayes' theorem: P(A|B) = P(B|A) x P(A) / P(B)
P(A) = prior, P(B|A) = likelihood, P(B) = evidence, P(A|B) = posterior (updated belief)
It updates the belief in hypothesis A when new evidence B arrives
Example: 1000 people, 10 sick; test catches 9 of 10 and flags 99 of 990 healthy; 108 positives, 9 truly sick; P(sick|positive) = 9/108, about 8%
Applications: spam filters, medical diagnosis, Naive Bayes classifier
